title: POC scoping - data handling for ApexCare Health
summary: POC scoping focused on PII handling, logging/redaction, retention, and prompt storage. Agreed on de-identified dataset for initial benchmarks, short retention for logs, and next-step security docs + demo of VPC option.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-06
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Kim (Redwood AE); Daniel Park (Redwood SE); Maria Lopez (ApexCare Head of Data); Raj Patel (ApexCare Security Lead); Nina Gomez (ApexCare PM)

00:00 Sophie: Thanks everyone for joining. quick intro — I'm Sophie, AE on the account, and Daniel is our SE. we'll run through POC scope focused on data handling, PII, logging and retention.
00:18 Maria: hi thanks. quick context — ApexCare is piloting patient triage assistant. For POC we want to test 1) accuracy on de-identified notes, 2) latency under burst traffic, and 3) that nothing sensitive leaks into logs.
00:30 Daniel: great, so the main knobs for us are hosted vs dedicated vs private. for data handling many customers pick Redwood Dedicated or Private so logs can be kept in customer-control, but we can also run hosted with strict redaction and short retention.
00:50 Raj: couple of constraints from security — must not store PHI in cleartext, and audit logs need to be available for 90 days for now; also need to prove we can redact PII at ingestion.
01:05 Sophie: understood. baseline question — for POC will you provide de-identified notes or raw PHI?
01:12 Maria: we'll provide de-identified for the first run, maybe a masked PHI set later in a controlled environment.
01:20 Daniel: good. recommended POC plan: use a de-identified dataset (5-10k rows) — run performance + quality benchmarks. configure logging to redact tokens matching patient identifiers at ingestion, instrument a separate retention bucket for logs (short TTL), and collect metrics (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, tokens per request, quality scores).
01:45 Nina: what's Redwood's redaction capability vs client-side redaction?
01:50 Daniel: we provide server-side configurable redaction rules (regex, entity lists) and can also accept client-side pre-redaction. caveat: automatic NER redaction sometimes over/under redacts; we recommend a combined approach: client-side masking for high-confidence PHI, server-side for additional scrub.
02:15 Raj: ok, and where are prompts stored? e.g., if an agent types a full note into the prompt, are those saved as plaintext?
02:22 Sophie: default behavior depends: on hosted API prompts and responses are logged in our telemetry for debugging unless you opt-out; retention defaults to 30 days but we can offer shorter windows for POC. for Dedicated, logs can be routed to customer-controlled storage and we support disabling persistent prompt storage — but short-term telemetry still exists for metrics.
02:46 Maria: would those logs be encrypted at rest with our KMS?
02:50 Daniel: yes — we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default; we can negotiate CKMS for enterprise deals.
03:05 Raj: SOC2? PCI? We need SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts to review for security team.
03:12 Sophie: we'll share the SOC2 report, pen test summary, and encryption docs — I'll attach security_deck.pdf.
03:20 Nina: for the POC success criteria, we want: 1) >=90% classification accuracy on test set, 2) p95 latency < 450ms for single-turn infer, and 3) no PII in logs per our sampling tests. timeline-wise we want a 3-week POC starting mid-October.
03:42 Daniel: sounds reasonable. on sizing — can you share expected QPS?
03:47 Maria: initial burst up to 25 rps, average 6 rps. typical request payloads are ~350 tokens, sometimes up to 1k tokens.
03:57 Daniel: for that profile we suggest a small dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalents) for predictable latency; for hosted we can try a benchmark run to see if latency SLOs hold under burst.
04:12 Raj: curious about prompt storage: if we disable prompt logging, will Redwood still retain any unencrypted KV cache or intermediate states that could contain user text?
04:22 Daniel: the KV cache is ephemeral per session; it is stored in memory on the serving nodes and not written to persistent logs. we do snapshot for debugging only when enabled. sometimes transcripts of streamed responses show up in debugging logs unless disabled.
04:40 Maria: you mentioned automatic redaction — how do we validate it? we need an auditable sample of raw vs redacted outputs for our compliance review.
04:49 Daniel: we can run a redaction validation job: feed sample inputs, store both original and redacted copies in a customer-only S3 with limited TTL for audit, and provide checksums. for hosted, we'd need a secure transfer; for Dedicated/Private this is simpler.
05:10 Sophie: ok next on retention — what's the minimum retention window you can support for telemetry/logs?
05:16 Daniel: we can set retention as low as 7 days on hosted; for POC we usually set 7-14 days. Dedicated/Private you control retention via your own storage lifecycle.
05:30 Raj: our compliance team prefers that prompts are not stored beyond 24 hours during tests. is that possible?
05:36 Daniel: we can configure a 24-hour TTL for logs for the POC on hosted but need a written agreement. also note that some operational caches and internal metrics may be kept longer in aggregated form.
05:52 Nina: regarding data access controls, can RBAC be granular per-route or per-team?
05:58 Sophie: yes — we support RBAC at route/model level in Redwood Console; for Dedicated/Private you can integrate SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning.
06:10 Maria: how do you handle prompt storage for analytics — e.g., if we want to keep anonymized prompts to improve prompts over time?
06:18 Daniel: two options: 1) store anonymized prompts (client-side masked) in your storage that we never ingest; or 2) use Redwood Optimize integrations to keep aggregated metrics and fingerprints of prompts (hashes) but not full text. storing full text means you own consent implications.
06:35 Raj: are there pre-built connectors for sending logs to our Splunk/Datadog?
06:38 Daniel: yes, we support forwarding telemetry to external sinks (S3, Splunk, Datadog). we'll share example configs.
06:48 Maria: talk through the benchmark plan — we need quality + perf + cost numbers.
06:52 Daniel: benchmark plan: 1) small warm-up with 500 requests, 2) steady-state run 10k requests at average 6 rps to measure latency and token cost, 3) burst test 25 rps for 2 minutes, 4) quality eval on 1k labeled examples. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens per request, model output quality (F1/accuracy), and cost per 1k tokens.
07:20 Nina: who will run the benchmark? Redwood SE or ApexCare?
07:23 Daniel: we'll run a joint run — Redwood prepares the harness and you provide the dataset and a test account. we'll record logs and metrics into the benchmark_spreadsheet.xlsx.
07:30 Maria: for quality scoring we prefer synthetic labels + human review. can Redwood help with sampling?
07:35 Daniel: yes we can provide sampling scripts and a human-in-loop review template.
07:42 Sophie: timeline recap: we can start mid-October if we get de-id data by Oct 13. week 1 — setup + baseline run; week 2 — benchmark runs + redaction validation; week 3 — analysis + stakeholder review. does that align?
07:58 Maria: yes that's fine. we may push some steps by a few days, but target mid-Oct start.
08:05 Raj: small security Q — will Redwood provide logs showing who accessed logs and when (audit trail)?
08:10 Daniel: yes audit logs are available; for hosted we provide an audit export, for Dedicated it's native in your control plane.
08:18 Nina: what about developer tooling — can our devs replay requests to reproduce bugs without exposing PHI?
08:24 Daniel: we recommend using hashed or tokenized prompts for replay. we also offer a replay mode that strips PII on export.
08:34 Maria: any gotchas on redaction coverage? e.g., patient IDs that are alpha-numeric and look like codes?
08:40 Daniel: those are tricky — regex rules help but you need example patterns. we recommend a combination of rule-based and whitelist/blacklist approach. we'll run a coverage report as part of validation.
08:56 Sophie: let's go over deliverables and owners (quick).
09:00 Sophie: Sophie — send security artifacts and POC template.
09:04 Daniel: Daniel — benchmark harness + redaction validation job + sample scripts.
09:09 Maria: Maria — supply de-identified dataset and sample PHI patterns.
09:13 Raj: Raj — internal security sign-off on 24-hour retention for POC logs.
09:18 Nina: Nina — schedule stakeholder review for Nov 6.
09:22 Sophie: great. any other concerns?
09:26 Maria: just one — we may need an NDA addendum around PHI during controlled runs.
09:31 Sophie: ok we'll loop legal; I'll include a note in next steps.
09:36 Daniel: final note — for cost modeling we'll provide an estimate of token unit cost for the benchmark and suggested dedicated sizing to meet latency targets.
09:44 Maria: perfect, thanks.
09:46 Sophie: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and calendar invites. end of call.
notes: Shared artifacts referenced: security_deck.pdf, sso_integration.docx, benchmark_spreadsheet.xlsx
Customer to provide de-identified CSV; Redwood to run redaction validation and benchmark harness
